question: Is CI on main getting slower?
short: Track how long a push to main waits for CI, and how many tests it runs, in any repository and language. Name the changes that made CI slower or faster, and the three that would cut the wait most.
lede: The wait that counts is wall time: from the first job starting to the last one finishing, not the job minutes added up. The skill charts that total with its slow tail, keeps each job's time to explain a step, records every step up or down as an incident with the change behind it, and keeps the three actions that would most cut the wait.
asks: How long does CI on main take?
Did CI get slower this week?
Record yesterday's CI figures in the CI Health Report.
steps: Reads GitHub Actions runs on the default branch, grouped by commit, for a UTC day or a backfill of up to 90 days.
Takes the median wall time of green pushes, a 7-day median as the headline with its spread and P95, and the share of run attempts that failed, re-runs included.
Reads the test count off the job logs, with patterns the agent writes for whatever runners the repository uses.
Optionally measures the test-to-code ratio over the main source directories, comments left out, and coverage when the repository defines mise run codecov.
Finds steps in wall time and stretches of hung runs, then names the change behind each from the PRs around it.
Keeps the top three actions that would most cut the wait, ranked by the minutes of waiting a day they could save, each with a button to discuss it in Claude Code.
With Uberblick, stores the day, the actions and any incident in the repository's own CI Health Report document: charts, then recommended actions, then incidents. Without it, prints a table.
facts: first job start to last job end, over every workflow of the push
the 7-day median with its ± and P95, so the slow tail shows
the share of run attempts that end red, per day and over 7 days, re-runs included
what the runners report, matrix copies counted once
test lines per code line over the main source directories, comments left out, and coverage through a mise task
the top three changes that would cut the wait, kept until done or outranked, each with a link to discuss it in Claude Code
the latest five changes that moved CI time, up or down
needs: python3 and an authenticated gh; the test count needs access to GitHub's job logs.

a local checkout for the ratio and coverage, with scc or cloc to count lines; the Uberblick MCP tools or the ub command, to keep the figures in a document; the Claude desktop app, to open an action's discussion.
one JSON file per repository and day, and the document's records.
